title: EVENT: Join University space experts for witness historic asteroid mission reveal - University of Liverpool News
excerpt: EVENT: Join University space experts for witness historic asteroid mission reveal
content:
Credit: NASA/Johns Hopkins APL

University of Liverpool’s space experts invite you to join them as the first images of NASA’s historic asteroid collision are revealed.

University of Liverpool’s space experts, led by Dr Stefania Soldini, invite students, staff and members of the public to join them for an exclusive first look at images revealing the aftermath of NASA’s historic asteroid collision.

Dr Soldini is a HERA team scientist and Director of the Zero-G Astrolab at the University of Liverpool.

On Wednesday 25 November, the European Space Agency (ESA) will unveil the first images from its Hera spacecraft, showing the impact following NASA’s 2022 mission to deliberately crash a spacecraft into Dimorphos, a small asteroid orbiting the larger asteroid Didymos.

Scientists will then find out exactly what happened when NASA’s DART spacecraft struck Dimorphos: Did the collision leave a crater, or did it dramatically reshape the asteroid?

The findings will provide important insights into how we could protect Earth from potentially dangerous asteroids in the future and how we can predict the aftermath of a kinetic impact.

You can join Stefania, Hera core science team member, and the UK Hera science team at the University of Liverpool, either in person or online, for a live connection with the ESA event in Berlin and the unveiling of these highly anticipated images.

Dr Stefani Soldini, Senior Lecturer (Associate Professor) in Space Engineering and UKRI FL Fellow, said: “This is a really exciting occasion and a fantastic opportunity to see what has happen to Dimorphos, for the first time, and the overall state of the Didymos system after the impact of the DART spacecraft. It’s a world first, and I encourage anyone with an interest in space, asteroids and the world beyond Earth to join us – either in person at the University or online – to be part of this momentous event.”

Join the Hera mission reveal

The ESA event in Berlin will bring together planetary defence experts and members of the DART and Hera mission teams.

A live connection with the University of Liverpool will allow attendees to share in the announcement and see the first post-impact images of Dimorphos as they are revealed.

Find out more and reserve your place: Hera Mission Arrival (online) Tickets, Wednesday, November 25  •  5:30 PM – 7:30 PM GMT | Eventbrite

Research findings

In a recent study, published in the journal of Astrophysics and Astrophysics, the Liverpool team show that the direction of impact affects the fate of debris and how this has my affected the system.

These findings offer valuable predictions for ESA’s Hera mission, which will investigate the aftermath of the DART impact and help scientists better understand how impact-generated debris evolves and redistributes across asteroid surfaces. Find out more about this study here.

Original Ideas Podcast:

Dr Soldini features in the latest Original Ideas podcast which focuses on Space research. 

The HERA Mission Reveal event is organised by Dr Stefania Soldini and Dr Ricardo Torres, and is sponsored by the UKRI-FLF Scheme grant number MR/W009498/1.
